day2_morning_wakeup_1.text: *The alarm goes off. I open my eyes. Day 2.*

day2_morning_wakeup_2.text: *The transfer papers I folded yesterday lie neatly at the edge of the desk. My bag is lighter than yesterday.*

day2_morning_wakeup_4.text: *My old school group chat. Below 'Read by 3,' only a new gray date divider has appeared. Still no replies.*

day2_morning_wakeup_6.text: *There's a message from Sea. 01:03. Her "Good night" notification sits right above the low-battery warning.*

day2_morning_wakeup_7.text: *I arrive at the school gate... and Sea is standing there.*

day2_morning_gate_1.text: Hey! I was waiting so we could walk together.

day2_morning_gate_2.text: ...You were waiting? What time did you get here?

day2_morning_gate_3.text: Just got here—I live right nearby. You've got cherry blossom petals stuck in your hair from the walk over.

day2_morning_gate_4.text: *Caked, dried mud clings to the toes of Sea's sneakers—hardly from walking straight down the paved main road from nearby.*

day2_morning_gate_5.text: *Sea lightly taps the toe of her sneaker against the pavement and, instead of answering, steps up right beside me.*

day2_morning_walk_1.text: What did you do yesterday? At home.

day2_morning_walk_2.text: Made some instant noodles, scrolled on my phone, then went to sleep. Nothing much.

day2_morning_walk_3.text: ...Do you eat instant noodles every day when you live alone?

day2_morning_walk_4.text: No, sometimes I get convenience store meals too.

day2_morning_walk_6.text: *Sea looks up at me with an unimpressed expression, then lowers her gaze to the empty water bottle in my hand.*

day2_morning_walk_7.text: I packed extra lunch today. Let's eat together at noon.

day2_morning_walk_8.text: Are you sure it's okay to do this much for me? I'm grateful just to walk to school with you.

day2_morning_walk_9.text: I keep ending up with extra anyway. It'd be a waste to throw it out.

day2_morning_walk_10.text: *Sea keeps walking ahead without turning back, her voice strangely bright.*

day2_morning_walk_11.text: Oh right, {name}, what kind of music do you listen to?

day2_morning_walk_12.text: I'm not picky. I listen to whatever sounds good.

day2_morning_walk_13.text: Me too. I've been listening to this singer a lot lately. The vocalist has a low voice.

day2_morning_walk_14.text:
*She shows me an indie band's channel.*

This one. The title might ring a bell.

day2_morning_walk_15.text: Oh, I know this song. It popped up in my algorithm once.

day2_morning_walk_17.text:
*Sea's scrolling thumb stops over the playlist on her screen.*

How did you know whether I tapped the heart? That's your phone.

day2_morning_deja4_1.text: *Sea turns off her screen and laughs it off. By the time we finish climbing the hallway stairs, my mouth is bone-dry.*

day2_morning_deja4_2.text: Hold on, where's the vending machine?

day2_morning_deja4_3.text: *Before I can say anything, my feet have already turned toward the second-floor stairs.*

day2_morning_deja4_4.text: Oh, right. There's a vending machine there. ...But {name}, how did you know that?

day2_morning_deja4_5.text: *The hallway sign is on the opposite wall. I’m already taking out my wallet before I even check that side.*

day2_morning_deja4_6.text: Oh, about that vending machine earlier—I must have seen it passing by yesterday.

day2_morning_class_2.text: *Sea smiles and slips her phone into her pocket. The tip of the thumb gripping its corner is white.*

day2_morning_class_3.text: *Morning homeroom. Ms. Eunsu opens the attendance register and calls out names one by one.*

day2_morning_class_4.text:
*A page of the attendance register turns. A chair leg briefly scrapes at the seat behind me. A girl sits in the back row with 'Seolhwa' written on her uniform name tag.*

Ms. Eunsu, didn't you miss a name in the back? I don't think you called it just now.

day2_morning_class_5.text: *The speaker above the blackboard gives a short buzz, and Ms. Eunsu turns to the next page. No one looks back.*

day2_morning_class_6.text: By the way, {name}, have you heard anything from your previous school?

day2_morning_pres_1.text: Transferring takes a while for the paperwork to go through. Let me know if they contact you.

day2_morning_pres_2.text: *First period, Korean Language. Ms. Eunsu writes the unit title on the blackboard.*

day2_morning_pres_3.text: Today we have group presentations. The topic is 'My Favorite Place.'

day2_morning_pres_4.text:
*Checking the group assignment sheet, I see the three of us are in one group—Sea, a boy I barely know, and me.*

Looks like the three of us are in the same group.

day2_morning_pres_5.text: Yeah! It says 'a place you like'—what should we do? We need to pick our topic first.

day2_morning_pres_6.text: A cafe or something? Honestly, anything's fine, right?

day2_morning_pres_7.text: How about the library? It should be quiet, and finding reference material would be easy.

day2_morning_pres_8.text: Nice. Should I make the slides?

day2_morning_pres_9.text: I'll present, and how about you look up the materials?

day2_morning_pres_11.text:
*Sea gives a thumbs-up. At the top of her notebook she's already written 'Library Presentation - {name}.'*

You already wrote the title? That was fast.

day2_morning_pres_12.text: *Prep time ends and our group gets called up. Once in front, the lines flow smoothly; Sea catches my eye each time right before I transition to the next point.*

day2_morning_deja5_1.text: {name}, great presentation. You must have presented a lot at your previous school.

day2_morning_deja5_2.text: Oh, yes. I did a few at my old school, too.

day2_morning_deja5_3.text: *When I thought of my old classroom, the windows and desks were there, but my seat in front of the board was left blank white. Even so, my palms weren’t sweating.*

day2_morning_deja5_4.text: *Break time. Ms. Eunsu walks over toward my desk.*

day2_morning_deja5_5.text: Settling in okay? You’re walking faster than yesterday.

day2_morning_deja5_6.text: *She gives my shoulder a light pat.*

day2_morning_deja5_7.text: *My shoulder feels cool where her hand rests, and a faint metallic whiff—like old copier toner—brushes past.*

day2_morning_deja5_10.text: Tell me right away if anything bothers you. I'm your homeroom teacher.

day2_morning_deja5_11.text: *Ms. Eunsu smiles and walks off toward the hallway.*

day2_morning_seolhwa_2.text: *Near the end of break, I glance behind me. My eyes meet Seolhwa's, sitting by the back window.*

day2_morning_seolhwa_3.text: *This time, she doesn't look away. She watches me without a word.*

day2_morning_seolhwa_4.text: *Her lips part just a fraction. Right before a single word slips out, a chair scrapes noisily across the front row.*

day2_morning_seolhwa_5.text: *The classmate beside me chatted while glancing back, though their gaze slid just to the right of Seolhwa. The next period's teacher walked in just then and tapped the lectern, calling out, "Focus!"—so I turned back to the front.*

day2_morning_pen_1.text: *Walking into the classroom and setting my bag down, I spot a brand-new pencil case on my desk with its paper tag still attached to the zipper.*

day2_morning_pen_2.text: It's a hassle keeping track of pens right after transferring, isn't it? I picked up an extra one.

day2_morning_pen_3.text: *Sea turned the pencil case lid towards me.*

day2_morning_pen_4.text: *Taking out the black pen, I draw a line on paper. The rubber grip where a thumb rests is faintly worn inward.*

day2_morning_pen_5.text: *Did you mix up what Sea used? The paper packaging was new, so there were no fold marks.*

day2_morning_pen_6.text: Use another one if the ink won't flow. I tried that one out in the shop.

day2_morning_pen_7.text: *When I turned the ballpoint pen, the pressed spot hit the thumb side of my left hand. I usually write with my right hand.*

day2_morning_pen_8.text: *I click the pen tip back in, click it out again, and sign my name. As my wrist adjusts, I notice which way the pencil case was turned.*

day2_morning_pen_choice.text: *Sea rested her chin on the desk and looked at the pen I was holding.*
choices: I hold it with my left hand.
Hold it with your right hand

day2_morning_pen_left_1.text: *When I switched to holding it with my left hand, the pressed groove stuck to my thumb. The pen did not turn even when I applied force.*

day2_morning_pen_left_2.text: *The ends of short horizontal lines drawn on paper trembled less than those drawn with the right hand.*

day2_morning_pen_left_3.text: You can write with your left hand too? I didn't know.

day2_morning_pen_left_4.text: *Instead of answering, I shifted the pen into my right hand. Maybe the childhood habit of doodling with both hands never quite wore off.*

day2_morning_pen_tease_1.text: *Sea touched the paper tag on the handle and stopped. The toes of my sneakers collided once under the desk.*

day2_morning_pen_tease_2.text: Yeah. I picked the best set in the stationery shop yesterday. Want to see the receipt?

day2_morning_pen_tease_3.text: *When I laughed it off as a joke, Sea tapped the cover of my textbook with the tip of her pen and told me to start by writing my name.*

day2_morning_pen_tease_4.text: *While writing my name, Sea took off the tag and put it in the trash. The paper was folded straight in two.*

day2_morning_pen_right_1.text: *I corrected it with my right hand and turned the grip half a turn, and this time my fingers slipped less.*

day2_morning_pen_right_2.text: Is that grip comfortable? If it isn't, we can go to the shop and exchange it.

day2_morning_pen_right_3.text: *I pull out the black ballpoint from the case and trace over my name. From the second stroke on, the ink flows evenly.*

day2_morning_pen_yuna_1.text: *Stepping into the hall before the bell, I find Yuna by the window wiping her camera lens with a microfiber cloth.*

day2_morning_pen_yuna_2.text: That's a new pencil case. Did Sea give it to you?

day2_morning_pen_yuna_3.text: *Asked how she knew, Yuna points to the tiny yellow price sticker on the side of the case—the local stationery shop's mark.*

day2_morning_pen_yuna_4.text: *The camera strap got caught on the corner of the window frame. When I stretched out my hand to take it out, Yuna was the first to cover the camera.*

day2_morning_pen_yuna_5.text: Oh, I'm sorry. It's pretty old, so the clasp on that side comes loose easily.

day2_morning_pen_yuna_6.text: *As I lowered my hand and stepped aside, Yuna wound the strap short around her wrist.*

day2_morning_pen_yuna_7.text: *From the classroom came the sound of chairs scraping back all at once. Yuna folded the cloth and slipped it into her pocket.*

day2_morning_pen_yuna_8.text: See you after class. And try not to lose your pen.

day2_morning_pen_eunsu_1.text: *I ran into the teacher by the hallway window. She had a box of chalk balanced on top of the attendance book, holding it with one hand.*

day2_morning_pen_eunsu_2.text: Done organizing your desk already? Yesterday you were still clinging to your bag even after the bell.

day2_morning_pen_eunsu_3.text: *When the chalk box tilted and I steadied it with my hand, the teacher tucked the attendance book under her arm and took hold of the box again.*

day2_morning_pen_eunsu_4.text: Thanks. You use your left hand really naturally too.

day2_morning_pen_eunsu_5.text: *I looked at the hand holding the box. It just so happened that the hand closest to me went out first.*

day2_morning_pen_eunsu_6.text: If that's a new pen, put your name on it. Plenty of kids use the same kind, so they get mixed up all the time.

day2_morning_pen_eunsu_7.text: *After getting paper to attach to the tip of a ballpoint pen and writing down my name, the teacher even handed me scissors.*

day2_morning_pen_eunsu_8.text: *I handed the scissors back to Ms. Eunsu and returned to my seat in the classroom. The warning bell rang, and Sea and I looked toward the front side by side.*

day2_history_callback_5.text: *I pull up Minsu's chat one more time. Seeing the unread mark still unchanged, I shut the screen right back off.*

day2_history_callback_6.text: *I told her the photo tucked into my notebook wasn't folded. Hearing that, Yuna loosened her grip on the camera strap a little.*

day2_history_callback_7.text: *When I mentioned that the app had been turned on again, the teacher told me to bring the installation instructions. I didn't put it off until tomorrow.*

day2_expansion_action_2_a.text: *I drew a line as a test with a black ballpoint pen. When the ink didn't skip, Sea tried writing her name in the blank space too.*

day2_expansion_action_2_b.text: *I pressed the lead of the mechanical pencil twice. Sea placed a blank piece of paper on the desk, saying it would break if it was pulled out too long.*
